question.text: A particle is placed at the origin and a force <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>kx</mi></math> is acting on it (where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi></math> is a positive constant). IF <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">U</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, the graph of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">U</mi><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mo>)</mo></math> versus <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></math> will be (where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">U</mi></math> is the potential energy function)

solution.text:
F = - dU dx       ⇒     ∫ dU = - ∫ Fdx

U 2 - U 1 = - ∫ kxdx   ⇒   U = - 1 2 kx 2
